**Application of animal genomics and data mining
to predict and monitor novel coronavirus
potential infections**

## Research team and collaboration

VirAnimalOne was coordinated by
[Prof. Luca Fontanesi](https://www.unibo.it/sitoweb/luca.fontanesi/en)
within the
[Animal and Food Genomics Group](https://site.unibo.it/animal-and-food-genomics/en)
at the University of Bologna.

I contributed to the research activities
as a member of the project team.

## Project overview

VirAnimalOne explored the use of animal genomic
sequencing datasets as an unconventional
source of information on viral sequences
and potential infections.

The project investigated computational
approaches for mining sequencing data
originally generated for animal genomics
rather than viral metagenomics.

These approaches can provide additional
information on animal-associated viromes
and support exploratory investigations
relevant to One Health.

## My research contribution

My research involvement focused on
computational approaches to the analysis
of animal genomic sequencing datasets.

The research activities are associated
with genome mining, bioinformatic
characterization of viral sequences
and interpretation of animal virome data.
